A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gC1qR contains two functionally distinct domains that can be recognized by MAbs and synthetic peptides.

MAbs 46 and 60 recognize an epitope in the NH2-terminal domain of gC1Q-r and are useful in identifying the gC1q-binding site on gC1q-r; and that MAbs 74 and 25 recognize epitopes in the COOH-terminal domain of gClq-r, which are distinct from the gC1Q binding site.

the NH2- and COOH-terminus of gCq-R contain functional domains that can be used to discriminate between the two forms of gCqR and to define epitopes that can be used for immunoprecipitation of the protein from cell lysates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NH2-terminal domain of gC1Q-r contains a binding site that is critical for C1q binding.
the C1q binding region of gC1Qr is located within the NH2-terminal 18 amino acids, and that the C-terminal 15 amino acids are involved in the binding to HMWK and Factor XII.
MAbs directed against gC1q-binding sites on gC1qR can distinguish between the two forms of gC1Q-r.
